Area.evidence_source: The metaphors that the interviewees use to describe their condition prior to the suicide attempt often relate to being alone in darkness. Expressions were noted, such as 'having been down in the basement and being dragged down by one thing or another', as well as references to an uncontrollable force, 'to lie below the ice and not be able to get up' and to being in a dark room 'where I cannot find the door; don't find the light switch'. Most tell about a condition where the darkness gradually increased and the decision to commit suicide emerged, 'I had simply given up'. For some, the decision was more abrupt, as a consequence of 'an immense feeling of hopelessness'. One interviewee describes his own condition as 'being inside a black cardboard box' and 'being surrounded by a totally black fog'. The person described how 'the bubble burst' when his condition changed from being 'completely up in cloud to turn into black' within 3 days, where the decision, 'I can't bear this', was taken. Also, another interviewee compares the condition with being in a black bubble: It's like I'm sitting inside a tiny bubble, a black bubble, that I'm the only one in there and no one else is able to get into it, and which I cannot get out of. When I'm so far down, everything is so black and dark that nothing can affect on you from the outside, because you enter a kind of psychosis. Several persons describe their longing for someone who is able to see, listen and understand. 'In my life I've never really had anyone who has been listening much', as one person said. 'It feels despairing not to be believed when you try to tell others about your depression'. To fight while suffering in solitude can be exhausting. The longing for someone to lean on, figuratively speaking, someone who can bring hope into periods when life is experienced without any flashes is understood as an essential element before, during and after the suicide crisis. Is it so that the deepest suffering experienced by the suicidal person is that of not being confirmed in his lonely struggle for life?
